problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 6 \\ 14\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{10\cdot (-2)+6\cdot 1+14\cdot 3}{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}}v=2[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{10\cdot 2+6\cdot (-2)+14\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}w=3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
